paragraphs: Walsall Council runs a not-for-profit fostering service, rated good by Ofsted, from Darlaston. It says it always tries to place children with its own carers first before looking at independent agencies such as those listed on this page.

Alongside short-term, long-term and family and friends fostering, the council runs an emergency scheme for young people, usually aged 10 to 18, who need a home at short notice, short breaks for young people with disabilities or complex needs, and New Horizon, which finds family homes for children aged about 10 to 18 who are living in children's homes. New Horizon asks for at least two years' experience with young people whose behaviour can be challenging and one carer based at home.

From April 2026 the council pays two weekly amounts: a household fee and an allowance for each child. The fee for one child is £246 a week, or £307 for advanced carers, and New Horizon Mockingbird carers receive £900. Child allowances run from £182 a week for under-fives to £267 for those aged 16 and over, with an extra week at birthdays and festivals and two weeks in the summer holidays. Carers living in the borough do not pay council tax, and those living outside get an equivalent payment. Our Walsall allowance page has the full table.

Support includes out-of-hours help, buddying, support groups and the Mockingbird fostering community. Carers already fostering elsewhere can transfer in as little as four months. Compare the council with two or three of the agencies below before you decide.
